rationale: Round 0 built and validated cleanly, so this round shifts weight toward stronger control-flow obfuscation: FLA gets the highest SecurityGain because the program is dominated by tiny, loop-heavy FP kernels (mandel, flops, whetstone, fbench) where flattening reliably destroys loop-structure signatures that reverse engineers key on, and BCF is close behind to insert opaque predicates into those same hot regions; both keep moderate RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so the dispatcher still throttles them on the innermost FP loops where overhead compounds. SUB and ICALL gain higher DiversityGain (SUB is cheap and bit-safe on the integer/control components of these kernels, and ICALL adds call-graph indirection in a program with only 6 functions where static analysis is already easy), while IBR stays mid-range to fragment branch structure without heavily taxing the benchmark loops. SPLIT remains a low-cost helper for size diversification. IGV is omitted: with 6 functions and ~1.4KB of text there are too few globals for it to add meaningful diversity, so its inclusion would only risk build complexity for no gain.
